study type: Preclinical experimental study (in vitro and in vivo animal model)
exposure: Polysialic acid loaded gelatin (PSA-Gel) composite hydrogels
PSA-Gel hydrogels cross-linked by tannic acid (TA) at 5%, 10%, and 15% concentrations
outcome: Antimicrobial behavior (against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli)
cohort: Rats with excision wound models were used for in vivo testing, alongside in vitro tests on bacterial strains and L929 fibroblast cell lines.
finding: PSA-Gel-TA hydrogels displayed strong antimicrobial behavior, favorable cytotoxicity, and significantly increased wound closure and healing rate in rats compared with native PSA-Gel hydrogels and untreated controls.
